# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 104 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 104 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_104_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 21

**1** "I saw the stones from those cast far from the tower: some lay in the rough field. **2** Others lay near the water; some were thrown off by the water and fell into it; others were cast away from the water and lay on dry ground. **3** Some lay in the mud and mire." **4** "I want to understand these things," I said, "what each of them means." **5** He answered me: "Those cast far from the tower and lying in the rough field — these are those who believed and then fell away entirely; they will not fit into the building, for they are like scattered rubble. **6** Those lying near the water — these are those who heard the word and wished to be baptized in the name of the Lord; but then they remembered the holiness of the truth and changed their minds, and went back to the desires of the wicked women." **7** "And those lying in the mud?" "These," he said, "are those who came to faith but then went back to the world and sought out their former way of life. **8** Some of these are still alive and others have already died. **9** For those still alive, if they repent quickly there is hope; but for those who have died, there is no hope — unless they are raised to life. But for the living — let them repent and not remain in their deeds, for they are in great danger." **10** He also showed me another place near the water — a great elevated open space, pure and clean — and those who were nearly whole were fitted in there and built into it. **11** And he said to me, "Come, let us go to the tower again and examine it." I came to the tower and sat there with him, and he said, "The tower is now complete; it cannot be enlarged any further."

---

*LOGOS: the "great elevated open space" near the water is the expanded Church territory — room for the nearly-whole who have repented. The tower's completion is final and absolute.*
